subject: Day 29: PURPLE crying primer; the 5 S's
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 29. PURPLE stands for Peak of crying, Unexpected, Resists soothing, Pain-like face, Long lasting, Evening clustering. It peaks at about six weeks and tapers by three to four months. Recognizing the pattern is half the recovery.

Action items
- Read the PURPLE crying overview together so both parents share the same mental model when the evenings are hard. Period of PURPLE crying program: https://purplecrying.info/
- Stock the kitchen for the evening hours; dinner that takes both hands does not work this week.
- Agree on a rotation for who handles the worst evening hours so the same parent is not on every night.
- If a feeding problem is suspected behind the crying — back arching, refusal, painful spit-up — message the pediatrician before the next visit. AAP HealthyChildren on crying and colic: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/crying-colic/Pages/default.aspx
- Continue the feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Evening cluster fussiness; pain-like facial expressions during crying that are NOT pain.
- [low concern] Hiccups and wet sneezing; quiet startle on loud sounds.
- [monitor] Forceful arching with feeds, painful spit-up, or feeding refusal — discuss at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] Bloody-mucus stool. Sustained feeding refusal. Persistent inconsolability paired with lethargy or fever.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Practice the 5 S's during a calm period so the sequence is ready for the harder hours: swaddle, side or stomach hold (only while held and awake), shush, swing, suck. AAP HealthyChildren on crying and colic: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/crying-colic/Pages/default.aspx
- Tummy time 20-30 minutes a day cumulative. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Take conversational turns with every coo during calm windows. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Outdoor stroller walk for 20-30 minutes most days — useful for both of you.

Upcoming
- Day 35-42: crying at or near peak.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit and first vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Calms when picked up or spoken to
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Early co-regulation. Not the same as stopping crying immediately — look for any shift in state.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calms-with-soothing/complete

- Briefly lifts head during tummy time
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Few seconds of head lift, even with bobble, counts. Builds neck strength for later head control.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brief-head-lift/complete
